title: Batch processing
subtitle: The same recipe applied to several images, one after another. The open image is not touched.

files.title: Images
files.explanation: FITS (including compressed), XISF, TIFF, PNG and camera RAW files. They are processed one at a time, in list order.
files.chooseFolderTitle: Folder of the images to process
files.noImagesInFolder: The selected folder contains no images that StarLight can open.

recipe.title: Recipe
recipe.explanation: What is applied to every image: Process tools, tone and color, curves, filter and file format. You can take it from the open image, save it and open it again.
recipe.takenFromImage: Values taken from the open image.
recipe.restartHint: Goes back to the starting recipe: Abracadabra on every file
recipe.name: Recipe name
recipe.abracadabraHint: Each image is measured and prepared as the Abracadabra button would do
recipe.abracadabraOn: Each image is measured and prepared as with the Abracadabra button: sky background, color, noise, detail, stretch and noisy edges are tailored to each one. With images that differ from each other, this is usually the best choice. The recipe’s filter, curves, vibrance and vignette are added on top.
recipe.abracadabraOff: The same fixed values for all images. Works well with similar images, for example from the same night and of the same object.
recipe.stretchPerFileHint: Black point, midtones and white point calculated for each image, as when you open it
recipe.stretchPerFileOn: Black point, midtones and white point are calculated on each image, as when you open it. Keep this on if the exposures differ.
recipe.stretchPerFileOff: Black point, midtones and white point stay those of the recipe for all images.

summaryList.processAbracadabra: chosen by Abracadabra for each image
summaryList.tonesAbracadabra: stretch and saturation measured by Abracadabra

framing.title: Framing
framing.edgesHint: Removes the noisy or empty edges measured on each image, as Abracadabra suggests
framing.aspectRatioHint: A centered box with the chosen shape
framing.fixedHint: The same crop for all images: it only makes sense with images that share the same framing
framing.fixedExplanation: The same portion ({width}% × {height}% of the image) is cropped in every file. Use it only with images that share the same framing, for example shots from the same session.

format.title: Output files
format.bits32Hint: Keeps the exact values, to continue working in another program
format.bits16Hint: Fine gradations, suitable for later retouching
format.qualityHint: Above ninety percent the loss is hard to notice.
format.keepMetadataHint: Copies the header keywords of the source file into the new file
format.markersHint: Draws the circles and names of the objects identified from each image’s capture data
format.caption: Caption with capture data
format.captionHint: This is the same option as in the Export step, where you also choose the template and the author. Each file gets its own data.

destination.title: Destination
destination.chooseFolderTitle: Folder where the output files are written
destination.tokens: {nameToken} is the source file name, {objectToken} the imaged object, {numberToken} the sequence number in the batch. For example {example}. An existing file is never overwritten: a number is added to the new one.

setup.waitForJob: Wait for the job running on the open image to finish.

progress.stoppingNote: Stopping: StarLight finishes the current phase, then stops the batch. The partly processed file is not written.
progress.stopNote: You can stop at any time: files already written are kept.
